title: I want to share my 2 cents on the bot farming crisis and my proposed solution

posts.cooked:
Hello! Forgive me if, at any point, this post comes off as hostile. I had a dissertation written out in notepad, but due to the forum restrictions, I could not paste it into this message and am now having to retype all of it.

First off, you can already see this is a wall of text. This post is not a troll, nor did I write it with AI (since it seems pasting text is forbidden, anyway). If you’re not interested in a personal introspection about the game’s bot/farming issue, then stop now and save yourself and all of us a headache by not replying. I don’t say that to be harsh, but to help all of us, including you, personally.

For context (you can skip this paragraph unless you’re curious), I am a casual player. I am playing Classic while waiting for Midnight, as my playtime priority goes to my retail guild. I’ve started dabbling in classic over the past few months since retail is on pause, so to speak, and I wasn’t super interested in Lemix. I’ve played WoW since late OG classic (a few months before OG TBC), and I’ve gotten to experience all the raids I missed back then, which has been exciting. Naturally, with everything “solved,” raids are objectively easier now than they were back then, but that’s unrelated.

On to the topic. The problem is obvious; gathering herbs or mining nodes is difficult (and in some cases, near impossible) due to bots roaming the landscape and snatching up the rarest spawns. RMT is a problem, although I am thankful that my classic toon is in a guild that strictly bans it. I do not RMT, nor will I ever, but there lies the problem.

I believe it is no exaggerationto say that the herb/mine system, at its core as it is now, is too bot-friendly. You can make arguments or conspiracy theories as to why that is, I know I have, but the only ones who know the truth as to why it remains unchanged are the Devs and the parent company. I’m not here to crap on them for it (despite believing it’s warranted), but the lack of action other than the alleged “banwaves” leaves much to be desired.

I want to take a moment now to outline my problem with the system as it is, how it affects my experience, and the solution/change I would recommend in order to improve things while hurting the Co.’s bottom line as little as possible.

~ My problem with the system ~

As a casual player, I basically cannot farm high-level herbs for my alchemy. I’ve tried, but the number of nodes I come across, given the time spent, is abysmal. In the case of black lotus, non-existent (I have played for around 4 months now and have only ever seen one, and that was before I got herbalism on a toon, so I guided another player to it). Since maxing out herbalism, I’ve put in multiple attempts for an hour or longer, at different times of day, but have yet to find/gather a BL, and all other herbs (in WP, Sili, BL and WS) are obscenely sparse.

I’m sure you’ve all read the anecdotes from players regarding RMTs; “Why would you farm for 10+ hours when you can buy what you need for the money you make in 1 hour?” pops up in a lot of posts I’ve gone through so far. What they don’t mention is the system that facilitates that exchange, and no one seems to suggest, “Maybe farming shouldn’t take 10 hours?” This is the issue that my suggestion below would theoretically address.

~ The effect on gameplay experience ~

Needless to say, everyone’s experience and priorities are different, so I will take this chance to again share mine. I want to be able to spend a reasonable amount of time gathering the resources I need to make the consumables I would use for raiding once or twice per week, and as it stands right now, I legitimately, literally can not do that.

As someone with disabilities in real life, my work prospects are severely limited. This makes the above issue hit way too close to home because the game makes me feel like I can’t get what I need to do what I really want (just like in real life). Yes, I know I can raid without consumables (to the chagrin of the RL’s, I suppose), but I want to contribute just as much as my guildmates, and it feels like I can’t because I’m a casual. Admittedly, they’re a little harder-core than I am, and they have alts dedicated to solo-farming in dungeons (i.e., mage), but I don’t have the time to prep for and do that sort of thing.

~ My idea for a solution ~

So, with all of that out of the way, this is what I would change if I had the option;

  • I would make it so that certain high-level nodes have a certain number of account-specific spawns that only one account has access to, capped each week.

To clarify, I would not make nodes only account-specific, as that would likely cause the market to explode, so open-world nodes would still spawn as they would normally. Additionally, these account-specific nodes would not be a “free handout” and would require time/effort to obtain, but that time/effort would be reasonable, not 10+ hours.

As a rough example, presume that hypothetically you need 6 black lotus (or fel lotus in tbc) to make the flasks needed to raid 6 hours a week. Each player account would have, say, 2 lotus spawns per zone (with the same respawn timer as they are now [15 minutes???]), and once they collect the 6th lotus, the account-specific nodes would disappear and not spawn again until the weekly reset. This example means that, given maybe 2 ish hours, a player can get the lotuses they need for the week, and if they want to get more to sell, then they have to compete with other players and unbanned bots.

Pros:

  • Casual players have an option to get what they need with “some” effort, minus the absurd frustration and unreasonable time investment, and are less likely to consider RMT.
  • Hardcore players can get what they need for their weekly raids much faster, and that would not only free up time for them either IRL or to do more stuff/farming in the game, but it would make them far less likely to consider RMTs to remain competitive.
  • Bot accounts missed by the alleged banwaves can continue to do what they do, meaning the corporate overlords won’t see a huge loss of subs. Again, that’s a conspiracy theory, but I’m just saying.

Cons:

  • Since every account is guaranteed at least some rare herbs/ore each week (with effort), said herbs/ore would be less rare. This would add more to the market, lowering the price.
  • It goes against the Classic gameplay ideal since it is changing how the system works.
  • It might feel like a handout.

I can see these being the main arguments against this idea, and in spite of how long this post is already, please allow me a moment to give my rebuttals.

“Rare trade goods are less rare, and the price will drop.” I presume with 99% confidence that the Devs have enough internal data to tweak the number of spawns-per-account such that it would allow players to get what they personally need without overextending and crashing that item’s price.

“It won’t be classic anymore.” This is true on the surface, but it’s literally the classic system that allows bots to control the market and hog everything. It cannot be fixed without changing it, I believe, and leaving things as they are/were to preserve that is, in my opinion, a fool’s errand, and is undeniably a source of stress/frustration among the player base.

“It’s just free rare herbs for every lazy scrub! You just don’t want to farm.” This is a bad-faith argument and ignores that players still have to go out and find them, as well as that each account (and therefore player) gets only the amount they personally would need, and anything past that point goes back to the old system (as broken as it is). The difference is that finding said rare herbs would be feasible and reasonable, at least until you have what you personally need.

I will end this post with this: I want to farm. I want, repeat, WANT the ability to go get what I need, but not when the time sink is impossible and there’s an actual, literal chance of zero success. I enjoy being able to get what I need together and make stuff; it’s why I liked the skinning/LW combo. As nice as it would be, I know I can’t ask the Devs to make the nodes work as they do in retail because I know there would be heavy backlash to that from the ClassicChads, so when I was trying to think of an alternative/middle ground that works for the most people, this is what came to mind. Thank you if you read this far, and I look forward to replies that provide constructive criticism or nods of agreement, if there are any.

Super edit: I shared this post with the classic guild I’m in and my GM even agrees. He farms a lot, and the upcoming changes to farming will only hurt players, not bots. His suggestion was a “currency” (like badges of justice, etc) that could be used to buy raid consumables or buffs that you get from just playing the game (like bronze in remix), so you can get what you need (to an extent) without being denied by bots.
